note: D16 re-checks the two headline claims under real seed variance (--shuffle). rx-only, K=4, max_epochs=8.

LR_peak_5e-4_vs_1e-3.verdict: NOT significant: diff=+0.00114 but Welch t=1.39 (df~2), p>0.2. The lr=5e-4 "peak" found in the single-seed D12/D13 sweep is INSIDE seed noise once lr=1e-3 variance (std 0.00141, ~8x that of lr=5e-4) is accounted for. Claim downgraded: lr in [5e-4,1e-3] is a plateau, not a peak. What IS robust is that both beat lr>=2e-3 (0.7650) and lr<=5e-5 (0.7109) by a wide margin.

soft_vs_sparse_routing.verdict: Significant: diff=+0.00938, Welch t=3.13 (df~3), p<0.05. top_k=K (soft) > top_k=2 (sparse) survives seed variance; sparse routing also carries ~2.4x larger seed variance.

meta_finding: Across every comparison, the WORSE configuration also has the LARGER seed variance (V2>V1, lr1e-3>lr5e-4, sparse>soft). Instability and inferiority co-occur, consistent with the gradient-mismatch diagnosis.
correction_note: An earlier reading claimed the LR peak was "6x the std" — that incorrectly used only the low-variance arm. Using the pooled standard error the LR claim does not survive; the routing claim does. Recorded here to keep the numbers auditable.
